newsitem.title: USA: CME opposes FASB decision on hedge accounting.
newsitem.headline: CME opposes FASB decision on hedge accounting.

text.p: The Chicago Mercantile Exchange said Monday it had urged the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB) to reconsider its latest decision on accounting treatment of hedging transactions.
The exchange was reacting to FASB's April 2 vote on the requirement of immediate recognition of current income from prior hedge gains or losses, it said.
"Hedging is a dynamic process, but the latest FASB position would put hedge managers in a virtual straitjacket," CME chairman Jack Sandner said in a statement.

"My fear is that the prospect of income volatility resulting from this ruling will have a chilling impact on the use of futures and other derivatives. This could encourage managers to ignore, rather than manage, risks."
CME president Rick Kilcollin noted in the statement that the revision on early hedge liquidation might be one of the most significant among the changes under FASB consideration.

"The CME is doing all we can to encourage the FASB to reconsider its latest position and revert to the accounting treatment for early hedge termination that was originally proposed in the Exposure Draft," Kilcollin said.

In an earlier Exposure Draft of rule changes FASB was considering, the accounting board recommended continuing the method of deferring hedge results until gains or losses for the cash flows underlying the hedge were recognized, CME said.

"The CME is concerned that the FASB made its decision without sufficient input from derivatives users," Leo Melamed, CME chairman emeritus, added in the statement. "We believe that if affected firms were given the opportunity to comment on this latest decision, they would overwhelmingly agree that the rule change is unwarranted."
FASB, an independent group that sets industry reporting standards, was due to finalize its controversial accounting rules for derivatives by June 30.

But last Friday, FASB director of research Timothy Lucas told a conference of derivatives professionals that the board may have to issue a new proposal instead of final rules by that self-imposed deadline.
